name: Aidon the Archwizard

facts.text: Level 75, 40,000 health, 30-40% resists, tether 1,500 (immune past it). A permanent Heat damage shield returns 100 per hit to melee attackers.

When first attacked he raises four Illusions of Aidon, fire, ice, air and earth (5,000 health each), whose area spells hit 300 in 350 around their target; he casts Aidon's Fire (500 Heat, radius 350) every 10-15 s. A new set comes 30-45 s after all four die, never while one lives.
Spawns of him exist in region 277 (Hall of the Corrupt) and region 233 (a later Summoner's Hall). Three bot lines put him in the Summoner's Hall.
'Archwizard: good for about two groups' (Feb 2003 Albion raid guide, likely him).

story:
Aidon was the best of Camelot's wizards in his day, and that is why the realm sent him to the Pennine watch: the Summoners' wards had to be understood before they could be broken. He found that the wards were not built of stone but of promises, and a promise can be read, and a promise can be answered. Whatever he promised in return, the Summoners kept their side of it. The watch died at its posts and rose facing the other way, and Aidon became the archwizard of the Hall, their gatekeeper on Albion's road. He mastered four elements in life and he wears them now as four reflections of himself, fire, ice, air and earth, and he calls a fresh set only when the last of the old set is broken. Those who see him in the Summoner's Hall itself are not mistaken. A gatekeeper is called to his masters' table now and then. Whose side is he on? His own, and theirs.

What he was sent to do. Aidon came to the Pennine watch with the realm's commission in his satchel and the best mind in Camelot behind his eyes. His orders were plain: learn the Summoners' wards, so that if Albion ever needed to close the road, it could. He took a tower in the hall and filled it with apprentices and candles, and for a season his reports were the most hopeful the Constable had ever read.

What he found. The wards were not stone but promises: the Summoners bind the dead and the living alike by bargains, and a bargain can be read, and a bargain read closely enough can be answered. Nobody knows what Aidon answered. The watch's clerk wrote that he stopped sleeping, that he asked for the watch to be doubled because he expected visitors, and that one night he came down from his tower with four of himself beside him. Whatever he promised, the Summoners paid. The watch died at its posts and rose facing the other way, and Aidon became the gatekeeper of the road he was sent to close.

How he fights. He mastered four elements in life and wears them now as four reflections: fire, ice, air and earth, each a full illusion of him, each casting a storm of its element around whoever it faces. He calls a fresh set only when the last of the old set is broken, as if he can only bear to make four new selves once the old four are all gone. He wraps himself in fire that burns whoever strikes him close, and throws great gouts of it into the ranks. Past the edge of his hall he cannot be touched; the Summoners' bargain keeps him at his post like any watchman.

Where he belongs. He is seen in the Summoner's Hall too, standing at Govannon's elbow as a steward stands at his master's table, and Albion's heralds have argued for years about which hall is truly his. The answer, the Camelot loremasters say, is both: he is the door between them.
legend: Two groups if you know the trick, the old guide said. When the fight starts Aidon splits into four reflections, fire, ice, air and earth, each with five thousand health and an area spell of its element around its target. Break three of them, one party each, and leave the fourth standing: he calls a new set only when all four are dead, thirty to forty-five seconds after the last one falls. Then everyone on Aidon. His fire shield burns melee for a hundred a hit, which adds up; healers on the melee. He throws a big fire blast into the raid every ten to fifteen seconds, so do not stack. Fight him on his own floor: past his tether he takes no damage and walks home, and the raids that dragged him spent ten minutes hitting a man who could not be hurt. If you see a fourth reflection standing at the end of the fight, nobody touch it until Aidon is down.

loremasterTopic.text: The realm sent him to study the Summoners' wards. He studied them too well. Four reflections attend him, fire, ice, air and earth. Break three and leave one; he calls them anew only when the last is broken.

bookPage: To the Constable. I do not know if this will reach you. The wizard came down from his tower tonight with four of himself walking beside him, one in fire, one in ice, one in air and one in stone, and he said that the visitors had come and that we should stand to. We stood to. Nothing came up the road. He looked at us very kindly, as a man looks at friends he has sold, and said that he had read the promise and answered it, and that we would all be kept. I asked him kept by whom. He did not answer.
